title: Attention opfusion profiling playbook
body:
Purpose:
Quick, shareable working playbook for profiling and validating attention operator fusion strategies across FlashAttention, paged attention, and fused kernel variants. Goal is to produce reproducible experiments we can attach to PRs and run in CI for regression detection.

Context / motivation:
- Recent regressions in long-context throughput for 8k and 32k workloads after introducing paged-attention routing (INF-2025). Some signals point to kernel launch overhead and increased L2 pressure when using fused ops.
- We want a small, deterministic experiment suite that isolates: kernel launch overhead, memory-bound vs compute-bound regimes, and multi-stream batching interactions.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked):
1) FlashAttention (FA) wins at medium context lengths (<=8k) when KV fits transient L2 partitions; paged attention wins at very long contexts due to reduced memory working set.
2) Simple fusion of softmax+matmul reduces kernel count but increases register pressure and spills on sm_80, causing slower runtimes on some shapes.
3) Fused kernels that don't respect per-block shared memory limits cause serialization at higher batch sizes.
4) Kernel launch overhead dominates for very small sequence lengths and/or high-concurrency tiny batch cases (continuous batching amplifies this).

Experiment matrix (to be run on representative GPU families: A100, H100, RTX6000 where applicable):
- Variables: model size (1B, 7B, 30B), seq_len {128, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768}, batch {1,4,16}, kv_cache_mode {cold, warm}, kv_page_size {4k, 16k, 64k}, attention_impl {flashattention, paged, fused-softmax-multi, fused-attn-opt1}, quant {fp16, bf16, int8-ptq}.
- Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency per request, GPU util, SM occupancy, L2 hit rate, global memory throughput (GB/s), allocated memory, kernel_count, average kernels per token.
- Repeat: 5 runs per cell, drop top/bottom latency to account for noise.

Commands / tooling notes:
- Use the local perf harness: ./bench/run_attention_profile.sh --model-size 7B --seq 8192 --batch 1 --impl fused-attn-opt1 --device cuda:0 --kv-mode warm --trace perf.trace
- Capture metrics: nvprof / Nsight Systems snapshots for detailed kernel timelines; nv-nsight-cu-cli --session .nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output out.qdrep
- Light-weight tracing for CI: ./serving/runtime/bench/mini_profile.py --impl flashattention --shape 1x2048 --iters 200 --save metrics.json
- Extract kernel list: nvprof --print-gpu-trace or use CUPTI-based kernel logger; map kernel names to our op-registry aliases.

Observations so far (raw notes from runs on h100-80gb):
- fusion variant 'fused-attn-opt1' reduced kernel_count from ~12->5 for 2048x1 but saw a 5-12% lower tokens/sec vs FlashAttention at seq=2048 for 7B.
- At seq=8192, paged-attention had 18-25% better effective throughput vs FA when kv_cache warm and kv_page_size=16k; with page_size=64k, memory allocation spikes and triggers occasional out-of-memory on 80GB config for batch>4.
- Nsight flamegraphs show increased register spills for fused-attn-opt1 on sm_80; blocks show lower achieved occupancy compared to FA kernels.
- Kernel launch stalls observed in multi-stream continuous-batching tests: many small kernels serialized across streams due to underlying CUDA stream priorities and implicit synchronization in our fused wrapper.

Diagnostics checklist (what to capture per failing experiment):
- full nsight timeline (qdrep) + exported csv of kernels
- nvprof kernel summary (time, calls, avg, percent)
- device free/used mem timeline (watch for fragmentation)
- counters: L2 hit/miss, dram_write_bytes, dram_read_bytes, achieved_occupancy
- PR link / commit hash used, docker image sha, commit tag for kernels/liba kernels

Root-cause signals to look for and how to validate them:
- Register spill -> validate with nvcc PTX or SASS report (nvcc --ptxas-options=-v) and check local compile flags for -maxrregcount tuning; compare regs per thread across implementations.
- Shared-memory overrun causing serialization -> instrument kernel entry to log shmem usage; run with smaller block sizes to see slope.
- Kernel launch overhead -> synthetic microbenchmark (single-GPU warm) that calls same kernel N times and measures amortized overhead; also test merging small word-size problems into single kernel.
- L2 thrashing -> run variant with forced prefetching or reduced page size to see L2 hit-rate change.

Lightweight reproducible case (put in CI):
- model: 1B, seq=2048, batch=1, impl=flashattention vs fused-attn-opt1
- command: python -m bench.attn_micro --model 1B --impl {flashattention,fused-attn-opt1} --shape 1,2048 --iters 400 --warmup 50 --out results.json
- compare tokens/sec and list top 3 heaviest kernels. If fused variant wins at tokens/sec but has >20% lower L2 hit, label 'memory tradeoff'.

Actionable changes we've prototyped:
- Add selective fusion flag at op-level: fuse_softmax_by_default=false; allow opt-in for specific shapes through a shape-dispatch table.
- Implement lightweight register-saver when compiling fused kernels to reduce spills at the cost of a little extra mem ops; toggled behind --fuse-regsave.
- For paged-attention: reduce default page_size from 64k->16k for H100 to avoid burst allocation; add autodetect of peak working set to choose page_size.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the perf delta consistent across model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder)? need cross-check with 2 encoder-decoder workloads.
- How does persistent-kv across many concurrent requests change the paging behavior? simulated concurrency tests needed.
- Do we need different default fusion heuristics per GPU ABI (sm_80 vs sm_90)? likely yes but need cost model.

Next steps (owners):
- (Maya) run the full experiment matrix on H100/staging for the 3 model sizes and upload artifacts to Confluence. Target: 2025-12-05.
- (Liam) add microbench that isolates kernel-launch overhead and wire to CI as quick-smoke. Target: 2025-11-18.
- (Sofia) prototype shmem/regs telemetry hooks in fused kernels and produce flamegraphs, attach to PR 987. Target: 2025-11-28.
- (Ethan) run cross-arch check on A100 and RTX6000 and summarize anomalies. Target: 2025-12-09.

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- remember to re-run with CUDA 12.3 vs 12.4 (I saw slight perf wobble on 12.4).
- talk to infra about dedicated h100 pool for longer runs (avoid noisy neighbor).
- possible quick win: disable fusion for seq<=256 by default.

References and context links: INF-2025 ticket, PR 987, existing confluence playbook (linked above).

If you're reading this and want to run a quick check: ping me and I'll add you to the staging H100 project. Copy this doc into PR description when you open an experiment change so reviewers have traceability.

-- maya
